configKeys.effect: Let beneficial splash/lingering potions be thrown while aiming at a tamed animal (vanilla swallows that right-click - the client reports CONSUME for any tamed wolf - so without this the potion never leaves your hand). Gates ONLY the pass-through half (PetPotionsModule.java:140): calming still works when this is false, you just cannot aim at the animal itself.

Effect ids (namespace:path) that make an angry owned animal forgive the player who threw the potion; works for splash and lingering potions alike. An empty list switches calming off entirely (isCalming returns false immediately) without affecting the throw-at-pets fix.
configKeys.range: elements must be String (defineList validator o -> o instanceof String); new entries default to "minecraft:instant_health"

configKeys.effect: How long (in ticks) a calmed animal refuses to re-target the thrower; 0 disables the grace period - the anger is still cleared once, it may just come straight back. Only one window per pet exists, so a second player's calm overwrites the first player's protection.

Play 4 heart particles above the animal and an amethyst chime (NEUTRAL, vol 0.7, pitch 1.5) when it is calmed, so it is visible that it worked. Fires only when anger towards the thrower was actually cleared.

notes:
DOCS STATE: there is no docs/modules/pet_potions.md - a repo-wide grep over docs/ finds no mention of the module at all. The only existing prose is README.md:37-38 (section "### Pet Potions"), and unlike most other README paragraphs it carries no "See docs/..." link. CHANGELOG.md 1.0.0-beta.65 (lines 539-568) is the richest existing source and is German.

SOURCE INVENTORY (5 files, all read in full): modules/pet_potions/PetPotionsModule.java (441 lines), modules/pet_potions/config/PetPotionsConfig.java (140), modules/pet_potions/models/CalmingCloud.java (record dimension+thrower), modules/pet_potions/models/PeaceEntry.java (record player+expiresAt), standalone/pet_potions/PetPotionsStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_pet_potions")), plus mixin/pet_potions/AreaEffectCloudAccessor.java. No DeferredRegister, no Commands, no KeyMapping, no recipe or loot hook anywhere in them.

SIDE, justified: side = both, and that is load-bearing, not incidental. The calming half is strictly server-side (explicit potion.level().isClientSide() at :169, event.getLevel().isClientSide() at :199, entity.level().isClientSide() at :362, plus ServerTickEvent.Post/ServerStoppedEvent). But the pass-through half (onEntityInteract :112-118 / onEntityInteractSpecific :125-131) carries no side guard at all and MUST take effect on the client - that is the entire point of the fix: Wolf#mobInteract returns CONSUME client-side for any tamed wolf (check is isTame(), not isOwnedBy(player)), which makes Minecraft#startUseItem bail before the use-item packet is ever sent (module javadoc :57-61, CHANGELOG "Ursache sass im Client" :562). The config is registered as ModConfig.Type.COMMON (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131, StandaloneModuleBootstrap.java:45), so the client really does have the values it reads there. A doc that calls this module "server-side" is wrong.

TWO DISTINCT CONCEPTS, easy to conflate in a doc:
- "beneficial" (isBeneficial :408-415) = no effect of category HARMFUL -> the throw is allowed to pass through the pet right-click. A splash potion of Swiftness is beneficial.
- "calming" (isCalming :418-431) = carries at least one effect id from calming_effects -> actually clears the anger. Swiftness is beneficial but does NOT calm. So "any good potion works" is false: only Healing/Regeneration (by default) forgive.
The two halves are independent in BOTH directions, which the first draft missed: a potion that calms but is not beneficial (a custom brew mixing instant_health with a harmful effect) is refused by the pass-through check yet still calms if it lands, and emptying calming_effects disables calming entirely (isCalming :419-421 returns false on an empty set) while the pass-through keeps working, because that path never consults the list.

GATING ASYMMETRY (missed by the first draft): only the pass-through half honours allow_throwing_at_pets - the check sits in shouldPassThrough (:140), not in the calming path. onProjectileImpact, onEntityJoinLevel, the sweep and the grace period check isModuleEnabled() only. Setting allow_throwing_at_pets = false therefore keeps calming fully alive (dispenser-fired splash, a potion thrown while not aiming at the pet, or any lingering cloud) - it only takes away the convenience of aiming at the animal itself.

TARGET SET: isOwnedPet (:399-401) tests instanceof OwnableEntity && getOwnerUUID() != null, deliberately NOT TamableAnimal. Per the module javadoc and CHANGELOG that is meant to cover horses, donkeys, mules and llamas (owner, but not tamables, hence not even vanilla's owner-targeting exemption) and modded pets; which vanilla classes implement OwnableEntity is a vanilla fact, not provable here. For a pet that is not a NeutralMob, calming only clears setTarget(null) / setLastHurtByMob(null) - there is no stopBeingAngry() to call (:304-316).

NO OWNER CHECK ON THE THROWER: calm() never asks whether the thrower owns the animal. Anybody the pet is currently angry at can buy themselves off, the owner included.

TARGETED PARDON: calm() (:298-332) only undoes anger aimed at the thrower (thrower.getUUID().equals(neutral.getPersistentAngerTarget()), mob.getTarget() == thrower, mob.getLastHurtByMob() == thrower). A wolf simultaneously angry at a third player stays angry at them. You buy off your own mistake, you do not pacify somebody else's guard animal. If none of the three matched, calmed stays false and the method returns before the grace period, the particles and the sound - so a potion thrown at a pet that was never angry at you produces no feedback at all.

REAL LIMIT - one grace period per pet: peaceWindows is a Map<UUID pet, PeaceEntry> (:78). Calming the same animal on behalf of a second player OVERWRITES the first player's window (calm -> peaceWindows.put(mob.getUUID(), ...) :323). Two players who both hit the same wolf cannot both hold protection at once.

STATE IS NOT PERSISTED: both peaceWindows and calmingClouds are plain in-memory HashMaps (:78, :81), cleared on ServerStoppedEvent (:384-388). A server restart drops every grace period - that part is certain. CORRECTION to the first draft: it also claimed a lingering cloud that survives the restart is "forgotten" for good. That does not follow from this repository. Tracking is armed from EntityJoinLevelEvent (:198), and whether NeoForge fires that event again when an AreaEffectCloud is deserialised from a chunk on load is a NeoForge/vanilla detail - if it does (and the cloud's owner resolves to an online Player), the cloud is simply re-tracked. Do not assert either way; see "unresolved".

LINGERING PATH: onProjectileImpact returns early for LingeringPotionItem (:173-175); lingering is handled purely via the spawned cloud, picked up in EntityJoinLevelEvent and re-swept every SWEEP_INTERVAL_TICKS = 10 ticks (:66, :240), so a pet that only wanders in later is still calmed. Two code-level conditions a doc should mention: the cloud is tracked only when cloud.getOwner() instanceof Player (:205) - a cloud with no player owner, e.g. one the server spawned itself, is never tracked; and the sweep skips a cloud for that tick when level.getPlayerByUUID(thrower) returns null (:268-271, continue, not remove) - the cloud stays tracked, it just does nothing while the thrower is not in that level. The sweep drops a cloud when its dimension is gone, the UUID no longer resolves to an AreaEffectCloud, or it is not alive (:264-267); onEntityLeaveLevel (:222-228) drops it as soon as it leaves.

GRACE PERIOD RATIONALE: clearing anger once is not enough - HurtByTargetGoal can re-fire off a stale lastHurtByMobTimestamp, and AI-overhaul mods set targets past vanilla's goals. The hook is LivingChangeTargetEvent (:356-377), i.e. Mob#setTarget itself, which is why it catches both. It cancels only when the new target is a Player whose UUID matches the stored PeaceEntry (:365-370), and it lazily drops an entry whose expiresAt has passed, measured against entity.level().getGameTime() (:372-375). CHANGELOG beta.65 (:558) names enhancedai as the motivating mod, but there is NO ModList.isLoaded check and no compile dependency anywhere in this module - it is not an integration, just the reason the generic hook exists. Do not list enhancedai as a supported mod.

CONFIG FALLBACKS: every accessor tolerates an unbuilt spec - isThrowingAtPetsAllowed() and isCalmFeedbackEnabled() return true when the value is null, getCalmingEffectIds() falls back to DEFAULT_CALMING_EFFECTS and getPeaceDurationTicksValue() to 200 (PetPotionsConfig.java:109-130). calming_effects is a defineList with element validator o -> o instanceof String and the new-entry supplier "minecraft:instant_health" (PetPotionsConfig.java:53-54). The class does not override isEnabledByDefault, so Module's default of true applies (core/Module.java:73-75).

DEAD CODE: getProtectedPets() (:438-440) is documented "for debugging and tests" but has zero callers in the whole repo (grep over src/, docs/, scripts/ finds only the declaration), and there is no src/test directory at all - src/ contains only main (the repo has no unit tests; see CLAUDE.md).

MIXIN: AreaEffectCloudAccessor is a read-only @Accessor("potionContents") on net.minecraft.world.entity.AreaEffectCloud - vanilla exposes only a setter, so there is no other way to ask a lingering cloud which effects it carries. Nothing in the module writes through it; the single call site is :208.

COPIED VANILLA GEOMETRY: the splash sweep re-implements ThrownPotion#applySplash by hand (inflate(4.0, 2.0, 4.0), distanceToSqr < 16.0; constants :69-75, use :183-188); the lingering sweep re-implements AreaEffectCloud#tick's cylindrical check (dx*dx + dz*dz <= radius*radius, :280-289). If Mojang changes those numbers, this module silently drifts out of sync with the real splash area.

MINOR, FLAGGED AS UNVERIFIED: expirePeaceWindows compares against server.overworld().getGameTime() (:244) while calm() stamps the expiry from mob.level().getGameTime() (:323) and onChangeTarget reads entity.level().getGameTime() (:372). Whether those are always the same clock across dimensions is a vanilla implementation detail (DerivedLevelData) that cannot be proved from this repository - worth knowing, not worth asserting in the docs.

FEEDBACK DETAIL: playCalmFeedback (:334-341) sends 4 ParticleTypes.HEART at y + 0.75 * height with spread 0.3/0.2/0.3 (ServerLevel only) and plays SoundEvents.AMETHYST_BLOCK_CHIME, SoundSource.NEUTRAL, volume 0.7, pitch 1.5.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSION: drinkable potions are not passed through (shouldPassThrough :146-148 requires SplashPotionItem or LingeringPotionItem), so holding an ordinary healing potion still lets you tell your own wolf to sit.

NOT GATED: onEntityLeaveLevel (:222) and onServerStopped (:384) do not check isModuleEnabled(); harmless, since both maps stay empty while the module is off. Note also that tickCounter (:240) only advances while the module is enabled, so the 10-tick sweep phase shifts after a runtime toggle - cosmetic.

WORDING DRIFT vs README: the code javadoc and CHANGELOG blame Wolf#mobInteract specifically; README.md:38 generalises it to "any tamed animal". The proven, code-level cause is the wolf one.

NO REGISTRY CONTENT: no items, blocks, entities, commands, keybinds, recipes, loot tables or lang keys - a grep over assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json finds nothing for this module, and src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml never mentions it. It is pure event logic plus one accessor mixin.

STANDALONE: build.gradle:452-453 lists pet_potions in standaloneModules as "Vanilla Plus: Pet Potions" with the one mixin and no clientMixins, no dataGlobs and no moduleDeps -> jar vpa_pet_potions, entrypoint standalone/pet_potions/PetPotionsStandalone.java, depends only on vpa_core (plus the generated neoforge/minecraft and incompatible-with-bundle entries).

HISTORY: the module directory was added in a single commit, f99284e ("chore(release): v1.0.0-beta.65", 2026-08-05), which is exactly what tag v1.0.0-beta.65 points at (git rev-list -n1 v1.0.0-beta.65 == f99284e7ac6b...). git log over modules/pet_potions/, mixin/pet_potions/ and standalone/pet_potions/ returns that one commit only - the module has never been touched since it was introduced.
oneLiner: Splash a potion of Healing or Regeneration onto someone else's wolf, cat or horse that you accidentally hit, and it forgives you instead of hunting you down until you die.
shortDescription: Throw a healing or regeneration potion at an angry tamed animal to make it forgive you, and let beneficial thrown potions actually be aimed at pets
